## 1. Script Purpose

Display a read-only, point-in-time snapshot of local TCP listening endpoints, showing their local address, port, and state.

## 2. PowerShell Code

```powershell
# Read-only snapshot of local TCP listening endpoints.
Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen |
    Select-Object -Property LocalAddress, LocalPort, State
```

## 3. Usage Example

If the script is saved as `LocalTcpListenerSnapshot.ps1`, run it from PowerShell:

```powershell
.\LocalTcpListenerSnapshot.ps1
```

## 4. Notes

- **Compatibility:** Requires PowerShell 5.1 or later on Windows with the NetTCPIP module available. Neither command relies on features introduced after PowerShell 5.1.
- **Permissions:** Uses the current session’s permissions. It does not request elevation; access restrictions remain unchanged.
- **Scope:** Queries only local TCP listeners. It performs no writes, downloads, remote-host queries, or configuration changes.
- **Output:** `State` should be `Listen`. Ports may appear multiple times for different addresses or address families. Results can change immediately after retrieval; this is not monitoring or a port scan.
- **Review status:** The three-line script meets the stated static acceptance criteria. It has not been executed or tested; runtime validation remains pending.
- **Microsoft documentation:** [`Get-NetTCPConnection`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/nettcpip/get-nettcpconnection) documents TCP retrieval and state filtering; [`Select-Object`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/select-object?view=powershell-5.1) documents property selection.
